name: s3scanner - S3 Bucket Permission Auditor
description: s3scanner discovers and audits S3 bucket permissions. It checks for public read, public write, and authenticated read/write on bucket and object ACLs. Finds exposed data, backup files, credentials, and source code in misconfigured buckets. Works against AWS S3, DigitalOcean Spaces, and any S3-compatible service.
notes:
=== INSTALL ===
  pip3 install s3scanner
  # Or: go install github.com/sa7mon/S3Scanner@latest

=== SCAN BUCKET LIST ===
  s3scanner scan --buckets-file buckets.txt
  # Checks existence, permissions, and lists objects

=== GENERATE BUCKET NAMES ===
  # Common patterns:
  echo "company-backup" >> buckets.txt
  echo "company-dev" >> buckets.txt
  echo "company-staging" >> buckets.txt
  echo "company-assets" >> buckets.txt
  echo "company-uploads" >> buckets.txt

=== DUMP BUCKET CONTENTS ===
  s3scanner dump --bucket <bucket_name> --output-dir loot/

=== AWS CLI ALTERNATIVE ===
  # List bucket (no auth needed if public)
  aws s3 ls s3://<bucket_name> --no-sign-request
  # Download everything
  aws s3 sync s3://<bucket_name> ./loot/ --no-sign-request
  # Check bucket policy
  aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket <bucket_name> --no-sign-request

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
- .env files, .git directories
- Database backups (.sql, .bak)
- Credentials and API keys
- Source code archives
- Customer PII / sensitive data
- CloudFormation/Terraform state files

references.title: MITRE T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage

recommended.note: enumerate-iam finds permissions; s3scanner finds exposed buckets.
Prowler checks S3 bucket configuration among many other things.

defense.why_it_works: S3 buckets can have ACLs that allow public or authenticated access. Many organizations accidentally expose buckets through overly permissive policies, bucket ACLs, or object-level ACLs.
defense.prerequisites: Target bucket names (guessed, enumerated, or found in source code/DNS).
defense.impact: Data exposure of sensitive files, credentials, backups, and customer data.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1530] S3 access logs showing anonymous or unusual access patterns; large data transfer from buckets.
defense.artifacts: S3 access logs; CloudTrail S3 data events; large outbound data transfer.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=aws sourcetype=aws:s3:accesslogs requester="-"
| stats count by bucket_name, operation, remote_ip
| where count > 10
defense.sentinel_kql:
AWSCloudTrail
| where EventSource == "s3.amazonaws.com"
| where UserIdentityType == "AWSAccount" or UserIdentityType == "Unknown"
| summarize count() by BucketName, EventName, SourceIpAddress
defense.prevention: Enable S3 Block Public Access at the account level; use bucket policies with explicit denies; enable S3 access logging; use AWS Config rules for public bucket detection.

detections.name: S3 bucket enumeration - anonymous access
detections.logic:
AWSCloudTrail
| where EventSource == "s3.amazonaws.com"
| where EventName in ("ListBuckets", "ListObjects", "GetObject", "GetBucketAcl")
| where UserIdentityType == "Unknown" or UserIdentityAccountId == "ANONYMOUS"
| summarize Operations=dcount(EventName), Objects=count() by SourceIpAddress, BucketName=tostring(parse_json(RequestParameters).bucketName)
detections.false_positives: Public website assets hosted on S3; CDN origin pulls
detections.tuning: Whitelist known CDN IPs; focus on non-public buckets
